def recipe_sha256(recipe: SyntheticRecipe) -> str:
    """Return the canonical SHA-256 provenance digest for a recipe."""
    document = recipe.model_dump(mode="json")
    if recipe.generator_version == 1:
        document.pop("noise_rms_fractional_gradient_xy")
        document.pop("invalid_rectangles")
    if recipe.generator_version < _CORRELATED_NOISE_GENERATOR_VERSION:
        document.pop("noise_correlation")
    canonical_json = json.dumps(
        document,
        allow_nan=False,
        separators=(",", ":"),
        sort_keys=True,
    ).encode("utf-8")
    return hashlib.sha256(canonical_json).hexdigest()

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: This page defines the terms the documentation, the code and the products use, in the sense Hebog gives them. Where a term has a different meaning in PyBDSF, Rapthor or LSMTool, the last section maps their name onto Hebog's. Each table links to the page where the term matters most.

docs.title: Images and headers
docs.text: Term Meaning FITS The file format of the input image and the output catalogue. An image file holds a two-dimensional array of pixel values and a header of keyword cards that describe them. See the input header contract. Header card One keyword, value and comment in a FITS header, such as BUNIT = 'Jy/beam'. Hebog reads the cards listed in the input header contract and refuses a card that does not hold the kind of value it should. WCS World Coordinate System: the header's mapping from pixel position to sky position. Hebog accepts an ICRS or FK5 J2000 celestial WCS and publishes every position in ICRS. ICRS, FK5 J2000 The two sky coordinate frames Hebog accepts. ICRS is the current standard frame; FK5 J2000 is the older frame many imagers still write, which differs from ICRS by a few tens of milliarcseconds. Right ascension, declination The sky's longitude and latitude, in degrees. Hebog publishes right ascension in [0, 360) and declination in [-90, 90]. Pixel One array sample. Arrays are indexed (y, x), row first; a pixel position written (x, y) is a coordinate for a WCS or a catalogue. Plane One two-dimensional image. Hebog analyses one plane; a FITS file with frequency or Stokes axes is accepted only when each has length one. Stokes I Total intensity, the only polarisation Hebog measures. A STOKES axis must select it. Reference frequency The frequency, in hertz, at which every published flux is defined. Hebog reads it from the image's frequency axis, RESTFRQ or RESTFREQ, or from the request when the header has none. MFS image A multi-frequency-synthesis image: one plane made from a whole band, reported at one reference frequency. Hebog's catalogue is an MFS catalogue with no spectral fit. Jy/beam Jansky per beam, the brightness unit of the input and of peak fluxes. A jansky is a unit of flux density; dividing by the beam makes it a brightness. Integrated fluxes are in Jy. Restoring beam The Gaussian blur every deconvolved radio image carries, written as BMAJ, BMIN and BPA in degrees. It sets the finest detail the image shows and the area that converts Jy/beam to Jy. Hebog applies one beam to the whole image and refuses one wider than 10 pixels. FWHM Full width at half maximum, the width used for the beam and for every fitted or deconvolved ellipse. The Gaussian sigma is the FWHM divided by about 2.355. Beam area The solid angle of the restoring beam, π × BMAJ × BMIN / (4 ln 2). In pixels it is about 1.13 FWHM² for a circular beam, which is why a minimum island of seven pixels is a fraction of a beam five pixels wide. Position angle The orientation of an ellipse's major axis, in degrees east of north, reported in [0, 180). Primary beam The telescope's sensitivity pattern across the field, highest at the pointing centre and falling towards the edge. It is unrelated to the restoring beam. Primary-beam-corrected image The image after division by the primary beam, so that fluxes are intrinsic but the noise rises towards the edge of the field. Rapthor calls it the true-sky image; it is an estimate, not truth. Flat-noise image The image before primary-beam correction. Its noise is roughly uniform across the field, so Rapthor uses it to estimate noise, and its fluxes are attenuated by the primary beam. Rapthor also calls it the apparent-sky image. Sector The part of the sky one Rapthor imaging run covers. Rapthor images each sector into a true-sky and a flat-noise image and runs the source finder once per sector. Invalid pixel A pixel that takes no part in any estimate or measurement: NaN or infinite, a stored integer equal to BLANK, or any pixel of a 3×3 square holding one repeated value, such as zero padding. The published RMS is NaN there. See invalid pixels. Supplied metadata A unit, beam or reference frequency given on the request with SuppliedImageMetadata because the header omits it. A supplied value never overrides a header value, and the diagnostics record it. Cut-out A rectangular region cut from a larger image, for example with Astropy's Cutout2D. Images above the size limit need one.

docs.title: Noise and background
docs.text: Term Meaning Background The slowly varying level of the image away from sources, estimated separately from the noise and subtracted before detection. The background setting is estimated (Hebog's spatial estimate) or zero (nothing subtracted, as PyBDSF's mean_map="zero"). RMS Root mean square: the local noise level, in Jy/beam, estimated from sigma-clipped pixels in windows and interpolated to every pixel. Hebog publishes it as rms.fits. Sigma clipping Repeatedly discarding the samples in a window that lie more than a set number of standard deviations from the rest, so that sources do not inflate the noise estimate. Hebog clips at three standard deviations. σ, signal-to-noise ratio Thresholds are multiples of the local RMS above the local background: a 5σ pixel is five times the local RMS above the background. Residual The background-subtracted image, image − background, on which Hebog detects, grows islands and measures. The residual of a fit is what is left after subtracting fitted Gaussians as well; the text says which is meant. Normalized residual The residual divided by the local RMS, so that each pixel reads in σ. Internal only; thresholds apply to it. Coarse grid The background and RMS grid of 150-pixel windows every 50 pixels, the same as PyBDSF's rms_box. Its values are interpolated to every pixel. Fine grid The RMS grid of 35-pixel windows every 7 pixels, the same as PyBDSF's rms_box_bright. The continuum profile measures it across the whole image on images at least 150 pixels on a side (local noise), and both profiles measure it around bright sources. Protected pixel, protected window A pixel that belongs to a candidate source is protected: it is excluded from the noise statistics, and a window that overlaps protected pixels is dropped. Clean window A noise window that overlaps no protected pixel and measured a noise above the noise floor. A dropped window takes the RMS of its nearest clean window, within the reach the RMS reference states. Bright region The area around sources at 75σ or more, where imaging artefacts make the noise change quickly. There the fine grid replaces the coarse RMS wherever it reads higher. Bright candidates close together chain into one region, estimated in bounded blocks. Noise floor The smallest spread a window can measure: the window's brightest absolute value times 2⁻²³, single precision's resolution there. A window under it measures no noise and is dropped. Unavailable RMS The state of a run in which no pixel has a finite positive RMS. The RMS product is all NaN and marked unavailable, the catalogue is empty and the mask is zero. It is not evidence of an empty sky. Flat-noise RMS The RMS of a sector's flat-noise image, published as flat-noise-rms.fits when the request names that image. Nothing else is measured on it.

docs.title: Detection
docs.text: Term Meaning Detection threshold detection_threshold_sigma: the signal-to-noise ratio an island must contain to be accepted. PyBDSF's thresh_pix. Island threshold island_threshold_sigma: the lower level to which an accepted island grows. PyBDSF's thresh_isl. It must be below the detection threshold. Seed A valid pixel at or above the detection threshold. An island needs a seed, or multiscale evidence over a minimum area in beams. Eight-connected Pixels joined through edges or corners. Islands and mask regions are eight-connected. Island A connected region of the published mask, and one row of the ISLANDS table. It can hold several sources, and a source can span several islands. Minimum island size minimum_island_pixels: the fewest pixels an island may have. PyBDSF derives its minpix_isl from the beam; Hebog requires it explicitly, and the Rapthor adapter applies PyBDSF's rule. Matched filter A beam-shaped smoothing filter whose response is highest where the image holds beam-sized emission. Hebog evaluates a bank of them to decide whether faint emission is significant. À trous wavelet, B3 spline A multiscale transform that separates an image into planes of increasing scale by repeated smoothing with a B3-spline kernel, without downsampling ("with holes"). Hebog uses scales 1 to 3 of the residual's transform as detection evidence; PyBDSF fits Gaussians to such planes. Scale One wavelet plane. Scale 1 holds structure about the size of the beam, and each later scale doubles that, so scale 3 holds structure about four beams wide. Multiscale support Pixels a detection gains from the filtered images rather than from its own thresholded pixels. It is kept only where it persists at an adjacent scale, and is assigned to the nearest detection along the emission within half a beam. Persistence A multiscale feature's appearance at two adjacent scales. Support that does not persist is dropped. Support, footprint The pixels a detection owns: its thresholded pixels plus any multiscale support assigned to it. Publication support is the part published in the mask. Owner The detection that owns a pixel. Every mask pixel has exactly one owner, decided by the detection, not by the tile that computed it. Parent One retained detection, with its support, as deblending receives it. Deblending splits a parent into components; one too large for the bounded deblend stays one component and is recorded as deferred. Mask source-mask.fits: 1 where a pixel is publication support, 0 elsewhere. Its connected regions are the catalogue's islands. It is not a CLEAN mask and not a photometric aperture.

docs.title: Components and fitting
docs.text: Term Meaning Deblending Splitting a parent into one region per significant peak, so that blended sources are fitted separately. Two peaks stay apart when the fainter lies at least 1.5σ above the pass between them. See compact deblending. Pass, saddle The highest level at which one connected part of an island still holds two peaks; the lowest point on the ridge between them. Deblended region The pixels that rise to one peak after deblending. It initialises one Gaussian fit; it is not yet a component or a source. Gaussian component One elliptical Gaussian whose fit was admitted, and one row of the GAUSSIAN_COMPONENTS table. Say "Gaussian component", because component alone can mean a clean or sky-model component. Moments The brightness-weighted centroid and covariance of a region's pixels. They initialise the fit and are never published as a fitted shape. Fit parent A group of components whose fitting regions touch, fitted jointly so that a neighbour's light is modelled rather than absorbed. A chain of more than sixteen components, or wider than the read budget, is fitted island by island instead. Joint fit One least-squares solve for every component of a fit parent at once, flagged joint-gaussian-fit. Free model, beam-constrained model The two Gaussian models a fit chooses between: a free ellipse, or one whose axes and angle are fixed to the restoring beam. A component takes the beam when its free fit is not significantly extended, reaches a bound or is ill conditioned. Admitted fit A fit that converged, stayed within its bounds, is well conditioned, leaves acceptable residuals and has usable uncertainties. Only admitted fits become Gaussian rows; a rejected fit keeps the detection and records why. Fit at bound A fit whose solution reached a configured limit on position, size or amplitude, flagged fit-at-bound; the component then takes the beam. Well conditioned A fit whose parameters the data can tell apart. A component that owns a few pixels along a line cannot fix its own width, so the fit is ill conditioned until that component takes the beam. Residual feature Positive emission left after subtracting a fit's Gaussians, grown from a detection-threshold seed and touching the fitted support. It makes a fit fit-model-inadequate, or joins components into one source. Beam deconvolution Subtracting the restoring beam's covariance from a fitted ellipse's to estimate the source's intrinsic size. See compact astrometry. Resolved, unresolved, major-axis-only The three deconvolution states: two significant intrinsic axes, none, or only the major axis. Only an unresolved source publishes a DC_Maj of zero in the Rapthor view. Extension significance Whether a fit is measurably larger than the beam: the log ratio of integrated to peak flux must exceed five times its uncertainty. A geometrically resolved fit that fails the test is unresolved, flagged extension-not-significant. Correlated noise Noise whose neighbouring pixels are not independent, because the beam smooths them. Hebog's published errors allow for it; its fit weights pixels by their RMS without modelling the correlation. Deferred The status of work Hebog did not do because an object exceeded a bound: a parent too large to deblend or fit stays one detection with deferred dispositions and no Gaussian. It is never silently dropped.

docs.title: Sources and the catalogue
docs.text: Term Meaning Source One or more components that Hebog associates as a single object in the image, and one row of the SOURCES table. Not necessarily one galaxy. Association The continuum profile's decision about which components form one source, from overlapping Gaussians, resolved arcs and loops, and shared residual emission. Each merge records its evidence in the diagnostics. The compact profile skips it. Association evidence The record of one merge: its reason (directional-fwhm-overlap, resolved-loop, resolved-open-arc or persistent-residual), the scales involved and the members. Segment The region a source is measured in: its support, expanded by a bounded aperture of 1.5 beams. Catalogue rows are measured one segment at a time. Association aperture A source's own non-overlapping region of the image. Each observable pixel contributes to at most one source's aperture. ASSOCIATION_APERTURE_FLUX The signed sum of background-subtracted pixels in a source's aperture, divided by the beam area, in Jy. Empty when the sum is not positive. Observed flux inside the footprint; no fit contributes to it. INTEGRATED_FLUX For a Gaussian component, the integral of its fitted Gaussian over the whole plane. For a continuum source, the sum of its components' integrals, PyBDSF's definition, or the aperture flux when no fit was admitted. See where the two source fluxes part. PEAK_FLUX A fitted Gaussian's peak amplitude in Jy/beam. A source of one fitted component publishes its component's; any other source publishes its brightest background-subtracted pixel. Position A single-component source publishes its Gaussian's fitted position and errors. Any other source publishes a centroid of its detection footprint, which can lie between two peaks or inside a ring, with no position errors. Catalogue row One row of the ISLANDS, SOURCES or GAUSSIAN_COMPONENTS table. A detection without a row still has a disposition in the diagnostics. Quality flag One of the comma-separated labels in QUALITY_FLAGS, such as resolved or aperture-flux-without-fitted-component. Readers must keep flags they do not recognise. See interpreting quality flags. Disposition The diagnostics' record of what happened to one component or source: measured, unavailable or deferred, the estimator, the reason and whether a row was published. Every detected identity has one. Estimator How a measured quantity was obtained: original-pixel-gaussian-model for a component, summed-fitted-component-flux or source-owned-signed-aperture for a source. Profile The reviewed set of algorithm settings a run uses: continuum (default, with association and local noise) or compact (one source per Gaussian, no association). Everything but the thresholds and island sizes is fixed by the profile. Reviewed science profile The packaged settings behind the profiles, reviewed_continuum_profile.json, whose SHA-256 the provenance records as scientific_profile_sha256. Configuration qualification The diagnostics label development-unqualified (the 5σ, 3σ, seven-pixel example settings) or custom-unqualified (anything else). Both mean Hebog is not qualified for survey use. Product One output file with its record: role, path, byte count, SHA-256, media type, schema version and scientific status. The readers verify the record before parsing. Bundle The output directory of four products, five with a flat-noise RMS, published together in one rename. Scientific status valid, or unavailable for an RMS product with no estimate. It says whether the file holds the quantity its role names. Provenance The diagnostics' identities of the run: SHA-256 of the input bytes, the configuration, the reviewed profile and the implementation, plus any supplied metadata. Scientific composition The implementation identity: a hash over every Hebog module the finder imports and every packaged resource. Two runs with the same input, configuration and composition give the same products. Run ID The caller's name for one run, carried into the catalogue and diagnostics. The same request with the same run ID returns its finished products instead of running again. Schema version The integer version of a record or file format. Readers reject versions they do not support; nothing is migrated before 1.0.

docs.title: Execution
docs.text: Term Meaning Executor The object that runs Hebog's tasks: SerialExecutor in the calling thread, ThreadExecutor on a pool of threads in one process, or DaskExecutor on a Dask client the caller owns. All three give the same products. See the executor contract. Serial reference SerialExecutor, the deterministic implementation every other executor and every tiling must reproduce byte for byte. Driver The process that called find_sources. It plans tiles, submits tasks, reduces their small results and writes the products; it holds no image-sized array. Worker A process or thread that runs tasks: a Dask worker, a thread of the pool, or the calling thread itself under the serial executor. Task One call of a function on one batch, submitted to the executor. Its arguments and result are small serializable records, never arrays the size of the image. Batch The unit of work one task receives: several tiles, or up to 256 objects whose reads fit a budget. Batching keeps the number of tasks proportional to tiles and objects, not pixels. Tile One rectangle of the image's grid, the unit of tiled work. Background and RMS use 128-pixel tile cores; every other stage uses 2,048-pixel cores, so an image up to 2,048 pixels is one tile there. Core The pixels one tile owns and writes. Cores do not overlap and cover the image exactly once. Halo The read-only margin around a core that a stage needs to compute the core's edge exactly, such as a filter's width. Each stage declares the smallest halo that makes its output exact. Stage One step of the finder in its own module under hebog.stages: background and detection, multiscale, support, publication, objects, association, sources, islands and catalogue rows, run in that order by composition.py. Pass One of the four groups of stages ADR-008 defines, A (noise), B (detection), C (support) and D (objects). A pass ends only where a global reduction must finish before any later decision. Round One map_batches call on the executor: one function over one set of batches, with one declared memory. A stage runs one or more rounds. Boundary summary The small record a tile task returns about its core's edges, such as the labels on each edge and each label's pixel count, bounding box and peak, so that objects crossing tile edges can be joined without sending pixels. Reconciliation Joining tile summaries into one global answer, such as one label for a region that crosses several tiles, through a pairwise tree fixed by tile order so that the result does not depend on completion order. Invariance The guarantee that tile shape, partition origin, worker count, task order and retries do not change the products. Tested by comparing one tile against an eleven-by-eleven grid and Serial against Thread and Dask. Read budget maximum_batch_read_pixels: the most pixels one object task may read. An object whose window exceeds it is measured from the cores that hold it instead. Wide object An object whose window exceeds the read budget: a filament crossing the image, say. The driver reduces it from the pixels its cores return, the one memory term that grows with an object rather than a tile. Declared memory The TaskRequirement every round states for its tasks: the measured cost per read pixel times the largest read, with headroom. The executor refuses a task larger than a worker admits and runs only as many at once as fit. Capacity ExecutorCapacity: the budget the caller admits, as worker count, threads per worker, tasks in flight and memory per worker. A DaskExecutor without one reads the cluster's current size. Resource names The names of the Dask worker resources, chosen by the caller, under which a DaskExecutor requests each task's declared memory and one core, so that Dask places tasks only where that much is free. Analysis memory What find_sources itself holds in the calling process, growing with the sources found, about 40 KB each, and with the image through the background's noise grids. hebog.analysis_memory_bytes states it for the caller to reserve, from the image's shape and the upper estimate of the source count that hebog.expected_source_count makes from the image. Generation One run's set of intermediate Zarr planes. It is complete only once an immutable marker names exactly one validated chunk for every plane and tile. Chunk One stored piece of a Zarr plane, one per tile core. A chunk is a storage unit; a tile is a work unit. Staging directory The hidden .<output name>.<random> directory beside the output in which a run builds its planes and products. A finished run removes it; a killed run leaves it with an owner record, which the next run to the same output reclaims once the owner has provably stopped. Atomic publication Writing the whole bundle into the staging directory, validating it, then moving it into place with one rename, so that a partial result is never visible. Secede A Dask worker task stepping out of its thread slot while it waits on other tasks, so that a waiting analysis does not block the tasks it submitted. Planned for Hebog's analysis inside a Rapthor task.

docs.title: Rapthor and sky models
docs.text: Term Meaning Rapthor The LOFAR calibration and imaging pipeline that is Hebog's first consumer. It runs on Prefect and Dask and uses PyBDSF today. Prefect The workflow framework Rapthor's main branch runs on. Rapthor's filter step is one Prefect task per sector. PyBDSF The Python Blob Detector and Source Finder, the finder Rapthor uses and the reference Hebog is compared against. Agreement with it shows compatibility, not truth. LSMTool The LOFAR sky-model tool. Its filter_sources keeps and groups sky-model components by the source finder's mask. filter_skymodel Rapthor's step that runs the source finder on a sector and then filters the sky model by the mask. See the Rapthor source-finding contract. Sky model The list of known sources, with positions, fluxes and spectral models, that a calibration pipeline predicts the visibilities from. WSClean writes one as a component list. Sky-model component One row of a sky model. Not a Gaussian component fitted by the source finder. Clean component One component the deconvolver (WSClean) placed while cleaning. Also not a fitted Gaussian component. Patch A group of sky-model components calibrated as one direction. LSMTool groups surviving components into patches by the mask's islands. Source-filtering mask What Rapthor and LSMTool do with Hebog's mask: keep the sky-model components that lie on detected emission. The mask is not a CLEAN mask, which controls deconvolution. Adapter hebog.adapters.find_sector_sources: the module that runs one sector through find_sources and writes Rapthor's file names and the eight-column catalogue view, importing no Rapthor, Prefect or LSMTool code. Eight-column view The Source_id, RA, DEC, Isl_Total_flux, Total_flux, DC_Maj, E_RA and E_DEC table Rapthor reads. See the Rapthor catalogue view. Fallback Rapthor's planned behaviour of running PyBDSF when Hebog raises a typed SourceFinderError. A refused sector leaves none of Hebog's files behind. Dual run Running both finders on one sector and comparing their products with compare_sector_products before choosing one set.

docs.title: Validation and evidence
docs.text: Term Meaning Injected truth Generated images whose sources' positions, fluxes and shapes are known, so that completeness, reliability and errors can be measured against an answer. Completeness, reliability The fraction of true sources recovered, and the fraction of reported detections that are true, for a stated population and matching rule. Quick science check just quick-science-check: 18 fixed cases compared with injected truth and pinned PyBDSF master, run on every scientific change. A regression detector, not qualification. See the contribution guide. Quick benchmark just quick-benchmark: five timed repetitions of the public finder per case, compared with the previous release and with PyBDSF master. Traced peak just traced-peak: tracemalloc's peak allocation in a fresh process, the figure memory gates use. Peak RSS is reported beside it as an envelope only. Release check The sequence of quick check, quick benchmark and traced peak run on a release candidate, whose results the progress page summarises. Equivalence lane just test-equivalence: find_sources and its stages against frozen PyBDSF products, run in CI. Contract test A test in tests/contract/ of a public behaviour, run through every executor. An unimplemented behaviour is a strict expected failure. Acceptance test A Given/When/Then test in tests/acceptance/ of a Rapthor-facing scenario. Anchor A fixed input the performance and memory figures are measured on, such as the 10,000² LoTSS-DR3 cut-out and the whole 15,402² mosaic. Performance ladder The frozen list of image sizes and workloads a release is timed on. See the performance contracts. Matched benchmark The deployment gate: Rapthor's complete filter_skymodel step with Hebog's native task against the same step with pinned PyBDSF master, in one container on the same cores and inputs. Measured by scripts/benchmark/measure_filter_skymodel.py (how to). Dataset role development for routine work, regression to preserve a decided case, or qualification, held out from tuning. See dataset manifests. Evidence record A versioned JSON document from hebog.validation.evidence that binds a measurement to its inputs, software and environment. reviewed only after its protocol and results pass review. Qualification Reviewed evidence that a frozen candidate meets the plan's gates on held-out data. No Hebog release has it; passing tests and development comparisons do not establish it.

docs.title: Naming conventions
docs.text:
• Use (y, x) for array shapes and indices, and names such as x_pixel and y_pixel where an interface takes (x, y).
  • Put the frame and unit in a name the type does not carry: ra_deg, beam_fwhm_deg, frequency_hz, flux_jy, flux_jy_per_beam.
  • Say detection_threshold and island_threshold; keep thresh_pix and thresh_isl only at the Rapthor boundary.
  • Qualify every component as gaussian_component, clean_component or sky_model_component, and never use source, island, Gaussian component, catalogue row and sky-model component interchangeably.
  • Say primary_beam_corrected and flat_noise; keep true_sky and apparent_sky where the Rapthor mapping is explicit.
  • Write catalogue in Hebog prose and modules; keep catalog in external field names and file names.
  • Name executors serial, thread and dask, as the classes are named.
  • A chunk is a storage unit and a tile a work unit; do not use one for the other.

docs.title: Evidence documents
docs.text:
Benchmark, traced-allocation and scientific-validation outputs use the strict versioned models in hebog.validation.evidence, so measurements keep their provenance without implying that an exploratory run passed a gate. hebog.validation is repository tooling, not installed from the wheel; use it from a source checkout after uv sync --all-groups.

Every document has schema_version (currently 1) and a discriminating evidence_type; a stable run identifier and timezone-aware timestamp; exploratory or reviewed status; the dataset identifier, role, content checksum, (y, x) shape and workload class; the exact configuration checksum; and strict fields that reject unknown data.

docs.title: Benchmark evidence
docs.text:
A benchmark document identifies the measured implementation by version and/or 40-character commit, container image digest where available and a checksum of the complete installed dependency inventory, with related Rapthor, LSMTool, Hebog or PyBDSF identities recorded separately; the environment has its own checksum so runs are never compared on display versions alone. Each repetition distinguishes warm-up from measured work and records wall and CPU seconds, peak resident memory, array-copy count and bytes, Dask task count, and transfer and spill bytes. Wall time, CPU time and peak RSS are required; optional instrumentation uses null only with a reason in unavailable_metrics, and zero always means a measured zero. A reviewed benchmark has at least one warm-up and five measured repetitions.

Resource records hold the executor kind, node/worker/thread topology, allocated cores, node memory, worker limits, reserved headroom and a storage identifier; aggregate worker limits must fit inside node memory after headroom. Reviewed multi-node evidence adds plane count, tile core and maximum halo, partition and graph task counts, scheduler overhead, worker occupancy, storage throughput, retries, stragglers and strong- and weak-scaling efficiency; separate documents per node count form the controlled scalability curve.

docs.title: Scientific-comparison evidence
docs.text: A scientific document identifies candidate and reference software separately and records a SHA-256 digest of each side's canonical product manifest plus the beam and match gate the comparison oracle used, so the report is bound to the exact catalogue, RMS and mask artifacts rather than to the input dataset alone. It embeds the complete product reports. Released PyBDSF and pinned master therefore produce separate documents even on the same dataset and candidate output.

docs.title: Writing and loading evidence
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path

from hebog.validation.evidence import load_evidence, write_evidence

write_evidence(Path("benchmark-results/run.json"), evidence)
reloaded = load_evidence(Path("benchmark-results/run.json"))

The writer sorts keys, rejects non-finite values, appends a final newline and replaces the destination only after writing a temporary file. load_evidence accepts benchmark, scientific-comparison and traced-allocation documents. A traced-allocation document, which just traced-peak writes, records each repetition's traced process peak, the peak of the find_sources call alone and the import floor; the contribution guide says when it counts as reviewed. Raw evidence stays under the ignored benchmark-results/ directory or controlled external storage; commit only compact reviewed summaries and reproduction metadata. The models expose model_json_schema(), and a breaking change bumps the integer version without migration support before 1.0 (ADR-006).

docs.title: Reference baselines
docs.text: config/baselines/ holds the reviewed compact and representative benchmark documents for released PyBDSF and pinned master, the reference-product manifest that binds the frozen PyBDSF products, the master-versus-release scientific comparison, the one-tile overhead record (the strict model in hebog.validation.overhead) and three inventories without a model: phase-0-reference-environments.json (sanitized package inventories, runner and compiler hashes, verified checkouts and the explicit 5.0/3.0 profile), phase-0-representative-dataset.json and phase-0-starting-revisions.json. A unit test loads every typed record through its model and requires the directory to contain nothing else. The master-versus-release comparison is written by scripts/validation/compare_reference_products.py, which the equivalence lane reruns against the committed record, so a change to the comparison oracle that moves it fails there.

docs.title: hebog.validation.evidence
docs.text:
Versioned machine-readable scientific and performance evidence.

Evidence documents distinguish exploratory observations from reviewed release evidence and distinguish unavailable instrumentation from measured zeroes. External product readers and benchmark runners create these records; loading this module never reads data or starts work.

docs.title: TRACED_PEAK_TOLERANCE_BYTES = 2 ** 20 // 10 module-attribute
docs.text:
Largest spread of traced peaks that still counts as one peak.

A traced peak repeats to a few kilobytes rather than to the byte, because the strings, paths and metadata of one run allocate slightly differently in the next. A tenth of a mebibyte is the precision a peak is quoted at, about ten times the spread measured across repetitions, and two orders of magnitude below the image-sized arrays a scalability change moves.

docs.title: BenchmarkEvidence
docs.text:
Bases: _EvidenceDocument

Versioned measurements for one exact implementation and environment.

Source code in src/hebog/validation/evidence.py 
class BenchmarkEvidence(_EvidenceDocument):
    """Versioned measurements for one exact implementation and environment."""

    evidence_type: Literal["benchmark"]
    subject: SoftwareIdentity
    related_software: tuple[SoftwareIdentity, ...] = ()
    environment_sha256: str = Field(pattern=_SHA256_PATTERN)
    resources: ResourceAllocation
    measurements: tuple[Measurement, ...] = Field(min_length=1)
    storage: StorageEvidence | None = None
    scalability: ScalabilityMetrics | None = None

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_benchmark_protocol(self) -> Self:
        """Enforce identity, ordering, and reviewed repetition requirements."""
        software_names = [
            self.subject.name,
            *(software.name for software in self.related_software),
        ]
        if len(set(software_names)) != len(software_names):
            raise ValueError("software identity names must be unique")

        repetition_indices = [
            measurement.repetition_index for measurement in self.measurements
        ]
        if len(set(repetition_indices)) != len(repetition_indices):
            raise ValueError("repetition indices must be unique")
        if repetition_indices != sorted(repetition_indices):
            raise ValueError(
                "measurements must be ordered by repetition index"
            )

        measured_repetition_seen = False
        for measurement in self.measurements:
            if measurement.warmup and measured_repetition_seen:
                raise ValueError(
                    "warm-up repetitions must precede measured repetitions"
                )
            measured_repetition_seen = (
                measured_repetition_seen or not measurement.warmup
            )

        if self.status is EvidenceStatus.REVIEWED:
            warmup_count = sum(
                measurement.warmup for measurement in self.measurements
            )
            measured_count = len(self.measurements) - warmup_count
            if warmup_count < 1:
                raise ValueError("reviewed evidence requires a warm-up")
            if measured_count < _MINIMUM_REVIEWED_REPETITIONS:
                raise ValueError(
                    "reviewed evidence requires five measured repetitions"
                )
            if self.resources.worker_nodes > 1 and self.scalability is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    "reviewed multi-node evidence requires scalability metrics"
                )
        return self

class ResourceAllocation(_EvidenceModel):
    """Admitted compute and storage topology for one measured run."""

    executor: ExecutorKind
    worker_nodes: int = Field(ge=1)
    workers_per_node: int = Field(ge=1)
    threads_per_worker: int = Field(ge=1)
    allocated_cpu_cores: int = Field(ge=1)
    node_memory_bytes: int = Field(ge=1)
    worker_memory_limit_bytes: int = Field(ge=1)
    reserved_headroom_per_node_bytes: int = Field(ge=0)
    storage_identifier: str = Field(min_length=1)

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_memory_admission(self) -> Self:
        """Keep aggregate worker limits within admitted node memory."""
        available_memory = (
            self.node_memory_bytes - self.reserved_headroom_per_node_bytes
        )
        admitted_worker_memory = (
            self.workers_per_node * self.worker_memory_limit_bytes
        )
        if available_memory <= 0:
            raise ValueError("reserved headroom must leave usable node memory")
        if admitted_worker_memory > available_memory:
            raise ValueError(
                "aggregate worker memory exceeds node memory after headroom"
            )
        return self

class RuntimeMetrics(_EvidenceModel):
    """Required timing/resource metrics with explicit unavailable values."""

    wall_seconds: float = Field(ge=0, allow_inf_nan=False)
    cpu_seconds: float = Field(ge=0, allow_inf_nan=False)
    peak_rss_bytes: int = Field(ge=0)
    array_copy_count: int | None = Field(ge=0)
    array_copy_bytes: int | None = Field(ge=0)
    dask_task_count: int | None = Field(ge=0)
    transfer_bytes: int | None = Field(ge=0)
    spill_bytes: int | None = Field(ge=0)
    unavailable_metrics: tuple[UnavailableMetric, ...] = ()

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_unavailable_metrics(self) -> Self:
        """Require one reason for every unavailable optional instrument."""
        metric_values: dict[OptionalMetricName, int | None] = {
            "array_copy_count": self.array_copy_count,
            "array_copy_bytes": self.array_copy_bytes,
            "dask_task_count": self.dask_task_count,
            "transfer_bytes": self.transfer_bytes,
            "spill_bytes": self.spill_bytes,
        }
        reason_names = [item.metric for item in self.unavailable_metrics]
        if len(set(reason_names)) != len(reason_names):
            raise ValueError("unavailable metric names must be unique")
        unavailable_reasons = {
            item.metric: item.reason for item in self.unavailable_metrics
        }
        for metric_name, value in metric_values.items():
            reason = unavailable_reasons.get(metric_name)
            if value is None and reason is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"{metric_name} is unavailable without a reason"
                )
            if value is not None and reason is not None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"{metric_name} has both a value and unavailable reason"
                )
        return self

class TracedAllocationEvidence(_EvidenceDocument):
    """Deterministic traced-allocation peaks for one input and configuration.

    ``tracemalloc`` counts the allocations the process itself makes, so its
    peak is reproducible for one input, one configuration and one
    implementation, which is why it, and not peak resident memory, gates a
    public envelope raise. Tracing roughly doubles wall time, so these
    documents record no timing that may be compared with benchmark evidence.
    """

    evidence_type: Literal["traced-allocation"]
    subject: SoftwareIdentity
    environment_sha256: str = Field(pattern=_SHA256_PATTERN)
    resources: ResourceAllocation
    measurements: tuple[TracedAllocationMeasurement, ...] = Field(min_length=1)

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_traced_protocol(self) -> Self:
        """Order repetitions, and require a reproduced reviewed peak."""
        indices = [
            measurement.repetition_index for measurement in self.measurements
        ]
        if len(set(indices)) != len(indices):
            raise ValueError("repetition indices must be unique")
        if indices != sorted(indices):
            raise ValueError(
                "measurements must be ordered by repetition index"
            )
        if self.status is EvidenceStatus.REVIEWED:
            peaks = [
                measurement.peak_traced_bytes
                for measurement in self.measurements
            ]
            if len(self.measurements) < _MINIMUM_REVIEWED_TRACED_REPETITIONS:
                raise ValueError(
                    "reviewed traced evidence requires two repetitions"
                )
            if max(peaks) - min(peaks) > TRACED_PEAK_TOLERANCE_BYTES:
                raise ValueError(
                    "reviewed traced evidence requires one reproduced peak, "
                    "within a tenth of a mebibyte"
                )
        return self

class TracedAllocationMeasurement(_EvidenceModel):
    """One traced repetition of one input through the public finder.

    ``peak_traced_bytes`` is the gate figure: the highest total of
    interpreter and NumPy allocations traced in the worker process, from
    before Hebog is imported until the products are written.
    ``finder_peak_traced_bytes`` is the peak over the ``find_sources`` call
    alone, measured from the same tracing session after its peak was reset,
    and ``import_traced_bytes`` is what the imports still hold when that call
    begins. Both make a peak comparable with one measured over a different
    span. ``peak_rss_bytes`` is an envelope, not a threshold: it varies with
    machine load, and tracing inflates it further.
    """

    repetition_index: int = Field(ge=0)
    peak_traced_bytes: int = Field(gt=0)
    finder_peak_traced_bytes: int = Field(gt=0)
    import_traced_bytes: int = Field(gt=0)
    peak_rss_bytes: int = Field(ge=0)
    traced_wall_seconds: float = Field(ge=0, allow_inf_nan=False)
    source_count: int = Field(ge=0)
    gaussian_component_count: int = Field(ge=0)

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_peaks(self) -> Self:
        """Require spans that one tracing session can have produced."""
        if self.finder_peak_traced_bytes > self.peak_traced_bytes:
            raise ValueError("the finder peak cannot exceed the process peak")
        if self.import_traced_bytes > self.finder_peak_traced_bytes:
            raise ValueError("the import floor cannot exceed the finder peak")
        return self

docs.title: Input header contract
docs.text: Hebog reads its physical description of an image from the FITS header. This page says what the public finder reads, where each value may come from, and how the headers that common radio imagers and pipelines write fare against it. Every image is either accepted or refused before analysis, with an error that names the keyword or layout at fault, or says that the file cannot be read as a FITS image.

docs.title: What the finder reads
docs.text:
Needed Read from When it is missing or unusable One image plane The primary HDU. The last two axes are the plane; every other axis must have length one. Refused, naming each longer axis, for example SPECLNMF (NAXIS3 = 16). Channel, Stokes and other cubes need their own contract. Stokes parameter A STOKES axis's world value at the plane, so a writer that encodes it in CRPIX rather than CRVAL is read correctly. No STOKES axis means Stokes I. Any parameter other than I is refused: Q, U and V, and instrumental planes such as XX or RR. A value that is not an integer parameter code, such as 1.4, is refused as malformed. Pixel values The plane's pixels in any BITPIX. A stored value is scaled by BSCALE and BZERO. A stored integer equal to BLANK is an invalid pixel, as NaN is, and so is every pixel of a block of one repeated value; see Invalid pixels. A file that ends before its last pixel is refused as truncated. BSCALE, BZERO and an integer image's BLANK must be numbers; see Numbers. Pixel unit BUNIT. Jy/beam is accepted in any case and with any spacing, as is Jy beam-1. A supplied brightness_unit, else refused. The public finder measures Jy/beam only, so any other unit or spelling, such as Jy beam^-1, is refused. A value without its quotes, which Astropy cannot parse, is refused. Restoring beam BMAJ, BMIN and BPA, in degrees. A supplied value for each missing keyword, else refused. A card that is not a number is refused; see Numbers. A beam wider than 10 pixels (FWHM) is refused; see Limitations. Reference frequency The first FREQ axis at the image's plane (its CRVAL when CRPIX is 1), then RESTFRQ, then RESTFREQ: PyBDSF's order, which reads no RESTFRQ. A supplied reference_frequency_hz, else refused. A card that is not a number is refused. Celestial WCS Astropy's reading of the header: any projection it supports (SIN, TAN, ZEA and others), with CDELT, a PC or CD matrix, or a legacy CROTA. Refused when absent. A card that is not a number, and a rotation Astropy would silently drop, are refused; see Numbers and Rotation. Coordinate frame The celestial axis types, which must be RA/DEC or GLON/GLAT, then RADESYS, EQUINOX and EPOCH. With none of the three, the frame is ICRS, as the WCS standard defines. EQUINOX or EPOCH of 2000 without RADESYS is FK5 J2000. Only ICRS and FK5 J2000 are accepted; the error names the frame found, such as GALACTIC or FK4, equinox 1950. Other celestial axes, such as ecliptic ELON/ELAT or supergalactic SLON/SLAT, are refused by their axis types, because Astropy would read ecliptic coordinates as ICRS. Catalogue positions are always ICRS. Size NAXIS1 and NAXIS2. Refused above 22,500 pixels on either side, and above 1,000,000 pixels in all when the shorter side is under 600.

Supplied values come from SuppliedImageMetadata on the request. Each one fills only a keyword the header lacks; supplying a value the header already has is refused, so a supplied value never overrides an image's own description. The diagnostics record every supplied value.

supplied = hebog.SuppliedImageMetadata(
    reference_frequency_hz=144e6,
    brightness_unit="Jy/beam",
)

docs.title: Imager and pipeline conventions
docs.text:
The table describes what each writer puts in the header, from its source code or documentation, and what the finder does with the header. Each row has a fixture test in tests/integration/test_input_header_contract.py. A header's result does not admit the image's size: an image larger than 22,500 pixels on either side is refused whatever its header. The whole LoTSS-Deep DR2 ELAIS-N1 and MIGHTEE XMM-LSS images, every LoTSS-DR3 mosaic and the 22,500² LOFAR-HD ELAIS-N1 mosaic fit; the finer LOFAR-HD mosaics and the full GLEAM-X and SDC1 images need a cut-out until the envelope reaches them.

Writer What the header holds Result WSClean Four axes: RA, Dec, FREQ, STOKES. EQUINOX = 2000 without RADESYS; the frequency is the FREQ axis's; BUNIT = 'JY/BEAM'; beam in degrees. Accepted as FK5 J2000. A polarisation product such as -XX-image.fits is refused as Stokes XX. DDFacet restored image, including the LoTSS-Deep DR2 ELAIS-N1 apparent and true-sky images Four axes with STOKES before FREQ; RADESYS = 'ICRS'; RESTFRQ; BUNIT = 'Jy/beam'; beam. Accepted. ddf-pipeline LoTSS mosaic (mosaic_pointing.py), including the LoTSS-DR2 and DR3 mosaics Two axes; RADESYS = 'ICRS' and EQUINOX = 2000; RESTFRQ = 144 MHz; BUNIT; beam. Accepted. ddf-pipeline generic mosaic.py Two axes; the beam copied from the first input image; no BUNIT and no frequency. Supply brightness_unit and reference_frequency_hz. The copied beam describes the first input only. LOFAR-HD ELAIS-N1 mosaics Two axes; BUNIT = 'JY/BEAM'; beam; no frame or frequency keyword. Read as ICRS; supply reference_frequency_hz. CASA exportfits Four axes: RA, Dec, FREQ, STOKES; a PC matrix; RADESYS = 'FK5' with EQUINOX = 2000, or ICRS; RESTFRQ when the image has one; BUNIT; beam. Accepted. An image with per-plane beams (CASAMBM = T and a BEAMS table) has no primary-header beam and is refused unless the beam is supplied. OSKAR imager Three axes: RA, Dec, FREQ; CROTA1 to CROTA3 all zero; no CUNIT; EQUINOX = 2000; BUNIT = 'JY/BEAM'; no beam. Supply the beam. OSKAR images are not deconvolved, so a supplied Gaussian stands in for the main lobe of the point-spread function. SKA SDP data models (export_to_fits) Four axes with STOKES before FREQ, the Stokes parameter encoded through CRPIX; RADESYS = 'ICRS'; beam when the image has a clean beam; no BUNIT or RESTFRQ. Supply brightness_unit; the frequency comes from the FREQ axis. Obit MFImage (MeerKAT SMGPS) Four axes whose third, SPECLNMF, holds the broadband image in plane 1, then spectral-index and sub-band planes (16 in an SMGPS tile); EPOCH and EQUINOX without RADESYS; BUNIT; the beam only as CLEANBMJ, CLEANBMN and CLEANBPA and in AIPS history cards. Refused as a cube. Plane 1 written as its own image is readable with the beam supplied from the CLEAN keywords, and the frequency too when Obit wrote no RESTFREQ. SMGPS mosaics are also in Galactic coordinates, which are refused. MeerKAT MIGHTEE DR1 (WSClean and DDFacet, mosaicked with Montage) Two axes in the TAN projection, yet CTYPE3 and CTYPE4 declare FREQ and STOKES axes with no NAXIS3 or NAXIS4; EQUINOX = 2000 without RADESYS; BUNIT = 'Jy/beam'; a circular beam. Accepted as FK5 J2000, with the frequency from the declared FREQ axis. The survey's effective-frequency maps, which give each pixel's own frequency, are not read. GLEAM-X DR1 mosaics (SWarp, then Miriad fits) Two axes in the ZEA projection; EPOCH = 2000; BUNIT and beam copied from one input snapshot; the frequency in a non-standard FREQ keyword. Read as FK5 J2000; supply reference_frequency_hz. The copied beam is not the mosaic's point-spread function, which the survey publishes as separate four-plane maps and which varies across the field; such a map is itself refused as a cube. SKA Data Challenge 1 (Miriad) Four axes; EPOCH = 2000; BMAJ and BMIN without BPA. Read as FK5 J2000; supply beam_position_angle_degrees.

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text:
Astropy and wcslib raise no error for a card that should hold a number and holds something else. wcslib warns and reads the keyword's default in its place, and a logical beam or frequency is read as the number one. A CRVAL1 of '180.0' would put every source at right ascension zero, a CDELT1 of NAN would make each pixel one degree wide, and a BMAJ of T would be a one-degree beam. Hebog refuses such an image and names the keyword.

The rule covers the restoring beam (BMAJ, BMIN and BPA), the reference frequency (RESTFRQ and RESTFREQ) and, on every axis, the numeric cards of the WCS: CRVALi, CRPIXi, CDELTi, CROTAi, PCi_j, CDi_j, PVi_m and its older spelling PROJPn, LONPOLE, LATPOLE, EQUINOX and EPOCH. Each must hold one finite number. None of these does:

  • text, including a quoted number such as '180.0' and an equinox written as 'J2000';
  • a logical, T or F;
  • a complex number;
  • NAN or INF, which FITS has no way to write, or a number too large to hold, such as 1.0E999; and
  • a number followed by its unit, such as 180.0 deg or 4 arcsec, or anything else that is not one number.

A WCS card with no value is refused too. A beam or frequency card with no value is a missing keyword, which a supplied value can fill.

The pixel scaling follows the same rule: BSCALE and BZERO must each hold one finite number, and BLANK, on integer pixels, an integer, as FITS requires. A scaling card with no value takes its FITS default. On floating-point pixels FITS gives BLANK no meaning, and it is not read. A scaling card that Astropy cannot parse at all stops the file from opening, and is reported as a file that cannot be read.

A number is read in any spelling FITS allows. That includes the D exponent that marks double precision, as in 1.8D+02: wcslib on its own stops reading at the letter and takes the value for 1.8, so Hebog gives it every float in the header, among these cards or not, as Astropy read it.

docs.title: Rotation
docs.text:
The WCS standard reads a legacy CROTAi rotation from the latitude axis only, and ignores it when a PCi_j or CDi_j matrix is present. Astropy follows the standard without a warning, so two kinds of header would be read with a different orientation than their writer intended, and every catalogue position would move. Hebog refuses:

  • a rotation on the longitude axis (CROTA1 for RA in axis 1) that is not zero and differs from the latitude axis's; and
  • a non-zero latitude-axis rotation beside a PC or CD matrix, in either its current spelling or the older PC001001 form.

A zero rotation, a rotation on the latitude axis alone, and equal rotations on both axes are unambiguous and accepted. OSKAR writes zeros; AIPS and Obit write the rotation on the latitude axis.

docs.title: Invalid pixels
docs.text:
A pixel is invalid when:

  • its value is NaN or infinite;
  • it is a stored integer equal to BLANK; or
  • it lies in a block of one repeated value: some 3×3 square of pixels that holds it holds one value. Every pixel of such a square is invalid, its edge as much as its centre.

An invalid pixel takes no part in the background, the noise, detection or measurement, and the published RMS is NaN there. Imagers and mosaicking tools mark a region they did not observe with NaN or with a constant, often zero. A constant region is not noise: a noise window over it measures a noise of zero, and one at its edge too little. PyBDSF's preprocessing stops with "Clipped rms appears to be zero" only when the sigma-clipped RMS of the whole image is about zero, as it can be for an image that is mostly zeros, and then asks for such regions to be blanked with NaN or cut with trim_box; a zero strip beside noise does not stop it. Hebog treats a block as blanked whatever share of the image it covers.

A block is blanked to its last pixel, as NaN padding is, so it leaves no step beside the data: a constant far from the noise, such as 1.0 Jy/beam beside noise of 10⁻⁴, or zero padding beside noise whose mean lies well below zero, publishes no island or source there. At the image edge a square is clipped to the image: a pixel at the edge is the centre of a square of one value when it equals the neighbours it has inside the image, five, or three at a corner. A block therefore reaches the edge, and a constant strip two pixels wide along an edge, or a 2×2 patch in a corner, is a block; a strip one pixel wide is not, nor is a constant line two pixels wide inside the image. NaN equals nothing, so a square that holds a NaN is not of one value, but a NaN inside zero padding leaves no zero valid, because other squares of zeros hold them. An image that is constant everywhere has no valid pixel, as an all-NaN image has none, and publishes the same empty products. Noise stored in steps much finer than its RMS does not repeat one value over nine pixels; an integer image quantized about as coarsely as its noise loses pixels to the rule (17% of one whose noise is about half a quantum).

The rule is one function, hebog.io.pixel_validity.valid_input_pixels. A pixel's validity depends on the pixels up to two away, so each window is judged from a read two pixels wider than itself, and the rule does not depend on how the image is tiled.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• One beam. Hebog applies one restoring beam, evaluated in pixels at the image centre, to the whole image. A mosaic whose inputs have different resolutions, or a wide ZEA mosaic whose projection changes the beam's pixel shape across the field, is not described by one beam. Measuring that effect and documenting how a point-spread function that varies across the field is handled is planned.
  • Frame defaults. A header with no frame keyword is ICRS. If its writer meant FK5 J2000, positions differ by the frame tie between the two, a few tens of milliarcseconds.
  • Header only. The contract checks what the header states, not whether it is true: a wrong BUNIT or beam is read as written.
  • Narrow images. An image whose shorter side is under 600 pixels may hold at most 1,000,000 pixels. The 150-pixel background meshes do not fit across so narrow a strip, and what replaces them reads the whole image in one task, which is bounded at that size.
  • Beam sampling. A restoring beam wider than 10 pixels (FWHM, major axis, to a thousandth of a pixel) is refused, under either profile and at any image size. The background and noise meshes are fixed in pixels, so a narrow noise window can take a wide source's emission for noise. On injected isolated sources every source at SNR 10 or more was published at beams of 3 to 10 pixels under both profiles; from 12 to 14 pixels the continuum profile missed some, and from 16 the compact profile. The limit is the widest beam measured with every such source published, not a bound on the cost of the analysis; beams between 10 and 12 pixels were not measured. Scaling the meshes with the beam would admit wider beams, and is deferred work. The measurement used circular beams and isolated sources; elliptical beams, blended or extended sources and crowded fields are not covered.
  • Repeated keywords. FITS does not define a keyword that appears twice, and Hebog does not refuse one. The WCS, including a frequency taken from its FREQ axis, is read from the last card of a repeated keyword, as wcslib reads it. The beam and RESTFRQ are read from the first, as Astropy reads them.

docs.text: The conventions above were read on 27 September 2026 from the writers' source code: WSClean's FITS writer in aocommon (include/aocommon/fits/fitswriter.h) and wsclean/io/wscfitswriter.cpp; DDFacet's DDFacet/Imager/ClassCasaImage.py; ddf-pipeline's scripts/mosaic.py and scripts/mosaic_pointing.py; OSKAR's oskar/imager/src/private_imager_create_fits_files.c; the SKA SDP data models' image_create.py and image_model.py; Obit's ObitImageMF.c, ObitImageUtil.c and ObitIOImageFITS.c, with Obit memo 63 and the SMGPS data-release paper (Goedhart et al. 2024); casacore's ImageFITS2Converter.cc and FITSCoordinateUtil.cc; and the GLEAM-X pipeline's SWarp templates. Headers read from the images themselves confirm the LoTSS-DR2 and DR3, SDC1 and LOFAR-HD entries (16 September) and the MIGHTEE DR1, GLEAM-X DR1, SMGPS and LoTSS-Deep DR2 entries (28 September).

docs.title: Internal API
docs.text:
This page is for developers working on Hebog. These modules are not a supported public interface and change without notice. The architecture overview explains how the layers fit together, and How Hebog finds sources explains the science.

The sections follow the order in which hebog.find_sources runs the stages. Each stage module applies pure kernels from hebog.algorithms and hebog.science with tiles, halos and executor batches, and hebog.stages.composition runs the stages in order; its first section documents it. hebog.science holds the reviewed profile and configuration, the composition records and the catalogue-row kernels; it imports no stage.

docs.title: hebog.stages.composition
docs.text:
The stage sequence find_sources runs, and the runner of each stage.

Each runner plans its stage's tile grid, opens the generation the stage publishes and runs the stage through the caller's executor. run_stages estimates the background and RMS and then calls run_stages_from_background, which runs every later stage in order on a published background and RMS; a caller that already holds one starts there instead of estimating it again. The sequence returns the generations and the records the terminal catalogues are built from, and builds no catalogue: hebog.public_science does.

docs.title: detect_multiscale_products(source, background_rms_source, executor, work_directory, *, image_shape_yx, beam, review, generation_id, tile_core_pixels=ADMITTED_TILE_CORE_PIXELS)
docs.text:
Run the tiled detection pass and read its published planes.

The composition owns no plane at all: the pass publishes what a later pass reads by window, and reduces each scale feature's peak while its response is still on the task that evaluated it. Only the reconciled island records come back.

tile_core_pixels is the non-overlapping output core each task owns. It defaults to the smallest core the scalability contract admits, and is widened when the widest filter halo would exceed a quarter of it. Tile geometry changes which task computes a value, never the value. One tile per batch is already a coarse task at that core, so batching adds nothing here.

Source code in src/hebog/stages/composition.py 
def detect_multiscale_products(  # noqa: PLR0913
    source: WindowReadable,
    background_rms_source: ZarrProductSink,
    executor: Executor,
    work_directory: Path,
    *,
    image_shape_yx: tuple[int, int],
    beam: BeamShapePixels,
    review: ContinuumScienceProfile,
    generation_id: str,
    tile_core_pixels: int = ADMITTED_TILE_CORE_PIXELS,
) -> tuple[ZarrProductSink, TiledMultiscaleDetection]:
    """Run the tiled detection pass and read its published planes.

    The composition owns no plane at all: the pass publishes what a later
    pass reads by window, and reduces each scale feature's peak while its
    response is still on the task that evaluated it. Only the reconciled
    island records come back.

    ``tile_core_pixels`` is the non-overlapping output core each task owns.
    It defaults to the smallest core the scalability contract admits, and is
    widened when the widest filter halo would exceed a quarter of it. Tile
    geometry changes which task computes a value, never the value. One tile
    per batch is already a coarse task at that core, so batching adds nothing
    here.
    """
    from hebog.algorithms.multiscale_tiles import (  # noqa: PLC0415
        scale_filter_halo_pixels,
    )
    from hebog.science.continuum import (  # noqa: PLC0415
        residual_detection_config,
    )
    from hebog.science.models import (  # noqa: PLC0415
        TiledMultiscaleDetection,
    )
    from hebog.stages.multiscale import (  # noqa: PLC0415
        MultiscaleStageConfig,
        run_multiscale_stage,
    )

    halo = scale_filter_halo_pixels(beam)
    core = max(tile_core_pixels, 4 * halo + 1)
    manifest = plan_image_partitions(
        image_shape_yx=image_shape_yx,
        tile_core_shape_yx=(core, core),
        halo_yx=(halo, halo),
    )
    sink = ZarrProductSink(
        work_directory / "multiscale.zarr",
        manifest,
        generation_id=generation_id,
    )
    result = run_multiscale_stage(
        source,
        background_rms_source,
        manifest,
        config=MultiscaleStageConfig(
            beam=beam,
            detection=residual_detection_config(review),
            maximum_tiles_per_batch=1,
        ),
        executor=executor,
        sink=sink,
    )
    return sink, TiledMultiscaleDetection(
        detection_islands=result.detection_islands,
        scale_islands_by_order=result.scale_islands_by_order,
        scale_nominal_beam_fwhms=result.scale_nominal_beam_fwhms,
    )

docs.title: estimate_background_rms(source, metadata, config, executor, work_directory, *, beam, review, generation_id)
docs.text:
Run the exact candidate-owned bounded background/RMS stage.

The stage publishes the background and the RMS as tiled planes, and the generation is what comes back: every later pass reads it by window. The one fact the composition needs about the estimate is whether any pixel can use it, which is reduced while streaming rather than kept as a mask. The diagnostics also record how far it refined around bright candidates.

Source code in src/hebog/stages/composition.py 
def estimate_background_rms(  # noqa: PLR0913
    source: WindowReadable,
    metadata: ImageMetadata,
    config: SourceFinderConfig,
    executor: Executor,
    work_directory: Path,
    *,
    beam: BeamShapePixels,
    review: ContinuumScienceProfile,
    generation_id: str,
) -> BackgroundEstimate:
    """Run the exact candidate-owned bounded background/RMS stage.

    The stage publishes the background and the RMS as tiled planes, and the
    generation is what comes back: every later pass reads it by window. The
    one fact the composition needs about the estimate is whether any pixel
    can use it, which is reduced while streaming rather than kept as a mask.
    The diagnostics also record how far it refined around bright candidates.
    """
    from hebog.science.configuration import (  # noqa: PLC0415
        source_finder_configs,
    )
    from hebog.stages.background import (  # noqa: PLC0415
        MultiscaleSourceProtection,
    )

    manifest = plan_image_partitions(
        image_shape_yx=metadata.shape_yx,
        tile_core_shape_yx=_TILE_SHAPE_YX,
        halo_yx=(0, 0),
    )
    sink = ZarrProductSink(
        work_directory / "background.zarr",
        manifest,
        generation_id=generation_id,
    )
    candidate_detection = source_finder_configs()[0]
    detection_config = replace(
        candidate_detection,
        source_finder=config,
        background_rms=replace(
            (
                _public_background_config(
                    metadata.shape_yx,
                    candidate_detection.background_rms,
                    source_finder=config,
                )
                if config.profile == "continuum"
                else candidate_detection.background_rms
            ),
            background=config.background,
        ),
    )
    detection = run_detection_stage(
        source,
        manifest,
        detection_config,
        executor,
        sink,
        protect_coarse_source_support=(
            config.profile == "continuum"
            and detection_config.background_rms.coarse.window_shape_yx
            != candidate_detection.background_rms.coarse.window_shape_yx
        ),
        refine_local_noise=(
            config.profile == "continuum"
            and min(metadata.shape_yx)
            >= max(candidate_detection.background_rms.coarse.window_shape_yx)
        ),
        multiscale_protection=(
            MultiscaleSourceProtection(
                beam,
                config,
                review.matrix.support_fraction_bounds[0],
            )
            if config.profile == "continuum"
            else None
        ),
    )
    return BackgroundEstimate(
        source=sink,
        usable_noise=estimate_has_usable_noise(source, sink, metadata),
        bright_regions=BrightRegionCounts(
            candidate_count=len(detection.adaptive_candidate_positions_yx),
            largest_read_pixels=(
                detection.background_rms_grids.largest_bright_region_read_pixels
            ),
        ),
    )

docs.title: estimate_has_usable_noise(source, background_rms_source, metadata)
docs.text:
Return whether any pixel has a usable local noise estimate.

This is the one decision the estimate makes about itself, and the only thing the composition needs from it: a pixel is usable where the image is valid and the estimate is positive. The stage has already required, on the core that computed it, that the estimate is finite wherever the image is valid, or, when no coarse window held enough samples for a background, nowhere, so validity is the image's own and needs no second opinion. The answer is reduced one canonical tile row at a time, so neither the estimate nor a mask over it is ever held whole.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If the published rows do not cover the image.

Source code in src/hebog/stages/composition.py 
def estimate_has_usable_noise(
    source: WindowReadable,
    background_rms_source: ZarrProductSink,
    metadata: ImageMetadata,
) -> bool:
    """Return whether any pixel has a usable local noise estimate.

    This is the one decision the estimate makes about itself, and the only
    thing the composition needs from it: a pixel is usable where the image is
    valid and the estimate is positive. The stage has already required, on
    the core that computed it, that the estimate is finite wherever the image
    is valid, or, when no coarse window held enough samples for a
    background, nowhere, so validity is the image's own and needs no second
    opinion. The answer is reduced one canonical tile row at a time, so
    neither the estimate nor a mask over it is ever held whole.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the published rows do not cover the image.
    """
    height, width = metadata.shape_yx
    rows = min(
        height,
        background_rms_source.manifest.tile_core_shape_yx[0],
    )
    usable = False
    start = 0
    for block in background_rms_source.iter_completed_row_blocks(
        "rms",
        max_block_bytes=rows * width * np.dtype(np.float64).itemsize,
    ):
        stop = start + block.shape[0]
        # Once a usable pixel is found, the image is read no further: the
        # remaining rows only confirm that the estimate covers the image.
        if not usable:
            window = source.read_window(ImageBounds(start, stop, 0, width))
            usable = bool(
                np.any(
                    window.valid_pixels
                    & (np.asarray(block, dtype=np.float64) > 0.0)
                )
            )
        start = stop
    if start != height:
        raise ValueError(
            f"background/RMS rows must total {height}; received {start}"
        )
    return usable

docs.title: publish_component_fits(source, background_rms_source, detection_source, component_source, executor, work_directory, *, image_shape_yx, beam, wcs_header_text, restoring_beam, config, review, component_count, generation_id, tile_core_pixels=ADMITTED_TILE_CORE_PIXELS)
docs.text:
Fit every measurement parent in its own context window.

Owners whose fit contexts touch need a joint model, so the contexts are reconciled first, a parent no joint fit can hold is split into its islands, and each fit parent is then measured inside the window holding it. The cores combine the persistent measurement support the parents contributed, and the connected features of that support are then grouped one window at a time.

Each parent also describes the direct components it owns, so the records the association decision reads come from the residual the fits already hold rather than from a second pass of per-component reads. component_count is the topology's, and the records must describe every one of those components.

Source code in src/hebog/stages/composition.py 
def publish_component_fits(  # noqa: PLR0913, PLR0917
    source: WindowReadable,
    background_rms_source: ZarrProductSink,
    detection_source: ZarrProductSink,
    component_source: ZarrProductSink,
    executor: Executor,
    work_directory: Path,
    *,
    image_shape_yx: tuple[int, int],
    beam: BeamShapePixels,
    wcs_header_text: str,
    restoring_beam: RestoringBeam,
    config: SourceFinderConfig,
    review: ContinuumScienceProfile,
    component_count: int,
    generation_id: str,
    tile_core_pixels: int = ADMITTED_TILE_CORE_PIXELS,
) -> tuple[TiledComponentFits, ZarrProductSink]:
    """Fit every measurement parent in its own context window.

    Owners whose fit contexts touch need a joint model, so the contexts are
    reconciled first, a parent no joint fit can hold is split into its
    islands, and each fit parent is then measured inside the window holding
    it. The cores combine the persistent measurement support the
    parents contributed, and the connected features of that support are then
    grouped one window at a time.

    Each parent also describes the direct components it owns, so the records
    the association decision reads come from the residual the fits already
    hold rather than from a second pass of per-component reads.
    ``component_count`` is the topology's, and the records must describe
    every one of those components.
    """
    from hebog.algorithms.component_measurement import (  # noqa: PLC0415
        fit_parent_margin_pixels,
    )
    from hebog.algorithms.multiscale import (  # noqa: PLC0415
        build_residual_atrous_plan,
    )
    from hebog.science.configuration import (  # noqa: PLC0415
        source_finder_configs,
    )
    from hebog.science.continuum import (  # noqa: PLC0415
        compact_deblend_config,
    )
    from hebog.science.models import TiledComponentFits  # noqa: PLC0415
    from hebog.stages.component_fits import (  # noqa: PLC0415
        ComponentFitStageConfig,
        run_component_fit_stage,
    )
    from hebog.stages.extended_groups import (  # noqa: PLC0415
        ExtendedGroupStageConfig,
        run_extended_group_stage,
    )
    from hebog.stages.fit_parents import (  # noqa: PLC0415
        FitParentStageConfig,
        run_fit_parent_stage,
    )

    _, _, moment_config, fit_config = source_finder_configs()
    fit_config = replace(fit_config, integrated_flux_bias_correction_sigma=0.0)
    atrous_plan = build_residual_atrous_plan(beam, noise_correlation=beam)
    context_margin = int(fit_config.context_margin_pixels)
    core = max(tile_core_pixels, 4 * context_margin + 1)
    fit_parent_manifest = plan_image_partitions(
        image_shape_yx=image_shape_yx,
        tile_core_shape_yx=(core, core),
        halo_yx=(context_margin, context_margin),
    )
    fit_parent_sink = ZarrProductSink(
        work_directory / "fit-parents.zarr",
        fit_parent_manifest,
        generation_id=generation_id,
    )
    run_fit_parent_stage(
        component_source,
        fit_parent_manifest,
        config=FitParentStageConfig(
            context_margin_pixels=context_margin,
            maximum_tiles_per_batch=_support_tiles_per_batch(
                fit_parent_manifest, executor
            ),
            read_margin_pixels=fit_parent_margin_pixels(
                fit_config, atrous_plan
            ),
            maximum_bounds_pixels=(
                compact_deblend_config(config).maximum_compact_bounds_pixels
            ),
        ),
        executor=executor,
        sink=fit_parent_sink,
    )
    manifest = plan_image_partitions(
        image_shape_yx=image_shape_yx,
        tile_core_shape_yx=(tile_core_pixels, tile_core_pixels),
        halo_yx=(0, 0),
    )
    sink = ZarrProductSink(
        work_directory / "component-fits.zarr",
        manifest,
        generation_id=generation_id,
    )
    result = run_component_fit_stage(
        source,
        background_rms_source,
        detection_source,
        component_source,
        fit_parent_sink,
        manifest,
        config=ComponentFitStageConfig(
            moment=moment_config,
            fit=fit_config,
            atrous_plan=atrous_plan,
            detection_sigma=config.detection_threshold_sigma,
            island_sigma=config.island_threshold_sigma,
            minimum_pixels=config.minimum_island_pixels,
            maximum_bounds_pixels=(
                compact_deblend_config(config).maximum_compact_bounds_pixels
            ),
            minimum_support_fraction=(
                review.matrix.support_fraction_bounds[0]
            ),
            maximum_tiles_per_batch=_support_tiles_per_batch(
                manifest, executor
            ),
            maximum_batch_read_pixels=_OWNER_BATCH_READ_PIXELS,
        ),
        component_count=component_count,
        wcs_header_text=wcs_header_text,
        beam=restoring_beam,
        executor=executor,
        sink=sink,
    )
    groups = run_extended_group_stage(
        source,
        background_rms_source,
        detection_source,
        component_source,
        sink,
        manifest,
        config=ExtendedGroupStageConfig(
            atrous_plan=atrous_plan,
            detection_sigma=config.detection_threshold_sigma,
            island_sigma=config.island_threshold_sigma,
            minimum_pixels=config.minimum_island_pixels,
            maximum_bounds_pixels=(
                compact_deblend_config(config).maximum_compact_bounds_pixels
            ),
            minimum_support_fraction=(
                review.matrix.support_fraction_bounds[0]
            ),
            maximum_tiles_per_batch=_support_tiles_per_batch(
                manifest, executor
            ),
            maximum_batch_read_pixels=_OWNER_BATCH_READ_PIXELS,
        ),
        parents=result.parents,
        wcs_header_text=wcs_header_text,
        beam=restoring_beam,
        executor=executor,
    )
    return TiledComponentFits(
        parents=result.parents,
        features=groups.features,
        component_records=result.component_records,
        wide_parent_count=result.wide_parent_count,
    ), sink

    label_source: ZarrProductSink,

    image_shape_yx: tuple[int, int],

    batch of segments measures their rows, their local noise and their moment
    shapes. The aperture plane stays in the published generation: the rows
    carry what the catalogue needs from it, so the driver never holds it.

        halo_yx=(0, 0),
    )
    sink = ZarrProductSink(
        work_directory / f"{sink_name}.zarr",
        manifest,
        generation_id=generation_id,
    )
    result = run_segment_row_stage(
        source,
        background_rms_source,
        detection_source,
        label_source,
        centroid_source,
        detection_source,

            label_product_name=label_product_name,
            centroid_product_name=centroid_product_name,
            aperture_radius_pixels=ceil(
                CONTINUUM_MEASUREMENT_APERTURE_RADIUS_BEAMS
                * beam.major_fwhm_pixels
            ),
            aperture_tie_policy=aperture_tie_policy,
            beam_area_pixels=(

                * pi
                / (8.0 * log(2.0))
                * beam.major_fwhm_pixels

    The owners a source holds are a record map, so the cores write the
    labels from the shard that reaches them; the support a source owns spans
    tiles, so it is reconciled before each connected component divides its
    unseeded pixels between the sources that seed it.
